thread:
Clare: FYI I ran a quick pass on PulseFinder-9B (baseline fp16) + int6/int8 quant sweep. posting unit-econ and QA notes.
Jason: Nice — did you use the same prompt suite as the GTN smoke?
Clare: Yes, reused GTN longform + summarization slices (slices: news-article, policy, howto).
Mohit: Quick headline? cost vs quality?
Clare: Headline: int6 saves ~48% token cost vs fp16, int8 saves ~30%. Quality: int6 shows small regression on long coherent summaries (4% ROUGE-L drop on news-article slice), int8 more stable but slightly higher latency.
Sara: 4% ROUGE-L is borderline for product. Do we have human evals for perceived harm/fluency?
Clare: We ran a 200-sample human A/B for news-article slice. int6 vs fp16: 18% of samples flagged as "shorter / missing context", 6% flagged as hallucination-prone. int8: 7% flagged shorter, 3% hallucination.
Elaine: So int6 has noticeable omission risk. Any pattern on prompt length / kv cache?
Clare: Yes — regression concentrated in prompts >1200 tokens. Likely kv-cache quant noise. Shorter prompts (<512 tokens) show parity across quant modes.
Jason: What about latency and p95 tail?
Clare: p50: fp16=85ms, int8=90ms, int6=78ms. p95: fp16=220ms, int8=260ms, int6=300ms. int6 tail jumps with long contexts.
Mohit: That p95 blowup is concerning for SLAs. Is that from extra CPU fallback or token re-issue?
Clare: Traced on runtime: long-context int6 falls back to fp16 for KV slice re-assembly in ~12% of requests which causes the tail.
Sara: Can routing policy mitigate? e.g., route long-context (>1k tokens) to int8 or fp16, keep int6 for short forms?
Clare: Exactly my proposal. Quick config suggestion:

```
routing:
  default: int6
  rules:
    - if: request.context_tokens > 1024
      target: int8
    - if: request.type == "summarization" and request.length_estimate > 512
      target: fp16
    - fallback: fp16
```

Mohit: Nice. What's the expected blended token-cost after that routing?
Clare: Simulation over full GTN traffic mix: ~35% of tokens hit int6, 50% int8, 15% fp16 -> blended token-cost down ~28% vs current fp16-only.
Elaine: And product risk? that routing should eliminate most long-context int6 tails and reduce the 18% human flags a lot.
Sara: For GTN recommendation, can we define a canary with live traffic split and quick eval hooks?
Jason: I'd add a quality SLO: monthly drift <2% ROUGE-L vs baseline and daily human-sample alert if regressions exceed 8% fail rate.
Clare: Proposal for GTN: 1) Canary 1% live traffic for 48h with full trace + GTN eval headroom. 2) If stable, roll to 10% for 72h with automated human-sample triggers. 3) Full roll only if daily quality alerts remain below threshold for 7 days.
Mohit: Ops note: for int6 canary, set runtime flag to disable kv-cache fallback to quantify tail cost if it remains. Also enable per-request exec-path logging.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: canary/pulsefinder/int6v1 -> env=canary, split=1% by user_id hash
Elaine: Also add a model-rollback policy: automatic rollback if p95 latency increases >40% OR daily human-flag rate >10%.
Sara: One more ask for the report: include sample-level examples where int6 trimmed content so product can review user-visible regressions.
Clare: Will attach 25 representative samples and the scoring spreadsheet to the GTN ticket.
Jason: Final rec for GTN deck wording? "Hybrid quant routing: default int6 for short contexts, int8 for long contexts, fp16 for sensitive summarization slices; expected token-cost reduction ~28% with controlled quality risk."
Sara: Agree. I'll draft the slide and include the human-sample snapshots.
Mohit: Thx Clare — great work. Any follow-ups I should own?
Clare: Can you own the canary infra (flags, logging) and coordinate with GTN for human review?
Mohit: On it.
Elaine: I'll own the rollback automation and SLO alarms.
Clare: Closing notes: next steps in ticket -> attach sample CSV, quant config, routing snippet, and cost simulation. Target decision review on Wednesday. :thumbsup:
Jason: +1
Sara: +1 :rocket:
